submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective locative/situating detector: fires on words that say where or by what something is situated or serviced -- strongest on passive ' served' (also ' run', ' held', ' covered', ' operated' weaker) right after 'is/was', on the comma right after a street address or room number ('Avenue,' 'Street,' 'Room 108,'), on spatial ' on'/' in' after a posture, occurrence or copular verb ('standing on', 'is on', 'shot in', 'go on', 'running on'; it fires there whatever follows), and on the place noun that closes such a phrase ('hallway', 'hall', 'floor', 'kitchen', 'room'). It is silent or weak on argument/idiomatic prepositions ('depends on', 'relies on', 'interested in', 'fond of', 'born in', 'based in'), predicate adjectives/nouns, and plain text without a placement phrase; there is no floor (the first token is ~0.08 of max).
